title: uber/causalml v0.18.0
summary:
This release **deprecates positional `treatment` and `y`** ahead of the v1.0 switch to `fit(X, y, treatment, ...)`, makes **causal trees and forests estimate leaves honestly by default**, and moves the **uplift trees and forests onto the shared Cython tree kernel**, with native missing-value support. It also adds benchmark dataset loaders with ground-truth metrics, new CATE evaluation scores, model `save()` / `load()`, and a rebuilt [documentation site](https://causalml.readthedocs.io/en/stable/) with an end-to-end tutorial, an estimator guide and an FAQ.

The full notes, with measurements, are in the [changelog](https://causalml.readthedocs.io/en/stable/changelog.html).

## ⚠️ Breaking Changes
* **`BaseSLearner.estimate_ate` always returns `(ate, lb, ub)` and no longer accepts `return_ci`.** `ate = learner.estimate_ate(...)` now binds a tuple, and passing `return_ci` raises `TypeError`; unpack instead: `ate, lb, ub = learner.estimate_ate(...)`. By @su-jin1425 in https://github.com/uber/causalml/pull/1031

## Deprecations
* **Positional `treatment` and `y` emit a `FutureWarning` (#854).** In v1.0 the positional order becomes `fit(X, y, treatment, ...)`, the scikit-learn convention. Pass both by keyword — `learner.fit(X=X, treatment=treatment, y=y)` — which is correct before and after the flip. A call left positional will silently train on swapped arguments at v1.0 rather than raise. See the [migration guide](https://causalml.readthedocs.io/en/stable/migration.html). B
